evidence_items.publisher: Nieman Journalism Lab; Renée DiResta, Abhiram Reddy, and Josh A. Goldstein
evidence_items.locator: Paragraph immediately before 'Generative AI meets scams and spam'
evidence_items.explanation: The authors describe their March investigation of more than 100 pages posting large quantities of AI images. This supports substantial proliferation and possible recommendation-driven amplification, but does not isolate moderation as its cause.

receipt.public_excerpt: We only included Pages that posted more than 50 AI-generated images.

evidence_items.explanation: The expanded study deliberately selected high-volume pages and cautions that they do not necessarily represent Facebook overall. Its sample cannot establish platform-wide prevalence or a causal effect of weak moderation.

evidence_items.locator: Section describing labels, removal policies, and fact-checking
evidence_items.explanation: Meta described existing moderation measures, including reduced distribution after adverse fact-checks. This qualifies a blanket account of absent enforcement, but supplies no independent measure of effectiveness.

unresolved_gaps: No representative estimate establishes the prevalence of AI-generated content across Facebook before the post.
The retrieved research does not separate the causal effects of moderation, recommendation algorithms, cheap content production, and financial incentives.
No retrieved enforcement comparison establishes how much stronger moderation would have reduced the observed proliferation.
